lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: # UI Prototype

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Generate **several radically different UI variations** on a single route, switchable from a floating bottom bar. The user flips between variants in the browser, picks one (or steals bits from each), then throws the rest away.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: If the question is about logic/state rather than what something looks like — wrong branch. Use [LOGIC.md](LOGIC.md).

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## When this is the right shape

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - "What should this page look like?"

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - "I want to see a few options for this dashboard before committing."

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - "Try a different layout for the settings screen."

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - Any time the user would otherwise spend a day picking between three vague mockups in their head.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## Two sub-shapes — strongly prefer sub-shape A

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: A UI prototype is much easier to judge when it's **butting up against the rest of the app** — real header, real sidebar, real data, real density. A throwaway route on its own is a vacuum: every variant looks fine in isolation. Default to sub-shape A whenever there's a plausible existing page to host the variants. Only reach for sub-shape B if the prototype genuinely has no nearby home.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ### Sub-shape A — adjustment to an existing page (preferred)

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: The route already exists. Variants are rendered **on the same route**, gated by a `?variant=` URL search param. The existing data fetching, params, and auth all stay — only the rendering swaps. This is the default; pick it unless there's a specific reason not to.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: If the prototype is for something that doesn't yet have a page but *would naturally live inside one* (a new section of the dashboard, a new card on the settings screen, a new step in an existing flow) — that's still sub-shape A. Mount the variants inside the host page.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ### Sub-shape B — a new page (last resort)

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Only use this when the thing being prototyped genuinely has no existing page to live inside — e.g. an entirely new top-level surface, or a flow that can't be embedded anywhere sensible.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Create a **throwaway route** following whatever routing convention the project already uses — don't invent a new top-level structure. Name it so it's obviously a prototype (e.g. include the word `prototype` in the path or filename). Same `?variant=` pattern.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Before committing to sub-shape B, sanity-check: is there really no existing page this could be embedded in? An empty route hides design problems that a populated one would expose.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: In both sub-shapes the floating bottom bar is identical.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## Process

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ### 1. State the question and pick N

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Default to **3 variants**. More than 5 stops being radically different and starts being noise — cap there.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Write down the plan in one line, in the prototype's location or a top-of-file comment:

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: > "Three variants of the settings page, switchable via `?variant=`, on the existing `/settings` route."

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: This works whether the user is here to push back or not.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ### 2. Generate radically different variants

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Draft each variant. Hold each one to:

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - The page's purpose and the data it has access to.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - The project's component library / styling system (TailwindCSS, shadcn, MUI, plain CSS, whatever).

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - A clear exported component name, e.g. `VariantA`, `VariantB`, `VariantC`.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Variants must be **structurally different** — different layout, different information hierarchy, different primary affordance, not just different colours. Three slightly-tweaked card grids isn't a UI prototype, it's wallpaper. If two drafts come out too similar, redo one with explicit "do not use a card grid" guidance.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ### 3. Wire them together

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Create a single switcher component on the route:

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ```tsx

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: // pseudo-code — adapt to the project's framework

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: const variant = searchParams.get('variant') ?? 'A';

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: return (

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: {variant === 'A' && <VariantA {...data} />}

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: {variant === 'B' && <VariantB {...data} />}

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: {variant === 'C' && <VariantC {...data} />}

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: <PrototypeSwitcher variants={['A','B','C']} current={variant} />

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: For sub-shape A (existing page): keep all the existing data fetching above the switcher; only the rendered subtree changes per variant.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: For sub-shape B (new page): the throwaway route under `/prototype/<name>` mounts the same switcher.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ### 4. Build the floating switcher

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: A small fixed-position bar at the bottom-centre of the screen with three pieces:

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **Left arrow** — cycles to the previous variant (wraps around).

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **Variant label** — shows the current variant key and, if the variant exports a name, that name too. e.g. `B — Sidebar layout`.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **Right arrow** — cycles forward (wraps around).

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Behaviour:

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - Clicking an arrow updates the URL search param (use the framework's router — `router.replace` on Next, `navigate` on React Router, etc) so the variant is shareable and reload-stable.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - Keyboard: `←` and `→` arrow keys also cycle. Don't intercept arrow keys when an `<input>`, `<textarea>`, or `[contenteditable]` is focused.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - Visually distinct from the page (e.g. high-contrast pill, subtle shadow) so it's obviously not part of the design being evaluated.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - Hidden in production builds — gate on `process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production'` or an equivalent check, so a stray prototype merge can't ship the bar to users.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Put the switcher in a single shared component so both sub-shapes can reuse it. Locate it wherever shared UI lives in the project.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ### 5. Hand it over

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Surface the URL (and the `?variant=` keys). The user will flip through whenever they get to it. The interesting feedback is usually **"I want the header from B with the sidebar from C"** — that's the actual design they want.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ### 6. Capture the answer and clean up

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Once a variant has won, write down which one and why (commit message, ADR, issue, or a `NOTES.md` next to the prototype if running AFK and the user hasn't responded yet). Then:

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **Sub-shape A** — delete the losing variants and the switcher; fold the winner into the existing page.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **Sub-shape B** — promote the winning variant to a real route, delete the throwaway route and the switcher.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Don't leave variant components or the switcher lying around. They rot fast and confuse the next reader.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## Anti-patterns

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **Variants that differ only in colour or copy.** That's a tweak, not a prototype. Real variants disagree about structure.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **Sharing too much code between variants.** A shared `<Header>` is fine; a shared `<Layout>` defeats the point. Each variant should be free to throw out the layout.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **Wiring variants to real mutations.** Read-only prototypes are fine. If a variant needs to mutate, point it at a stub — the question is "what should this look like", not "does the backend work".

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **Promoting the prototype directly to production.** The variant code was written under prototype constraints (no tests, minimal error handling). Rewrite it properly when you fold it in.
